subject: Cryptographic handshake & rotation checklist for Nimbus Health RFI
messages:
From: Priya Ramesh <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Turner <security_engineer@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cryptography section clarifications / request for network diagram

Marissa,

Thanks for the initial RFI response — our procurement/security teams have a few clarifying questions specific to KMS/HSM and rotation so we can complete the vendor risk review for Nimbus Health. Can you confirm the following and share any schematic/network diagrams and a sample rotation schedule?

1) BYOK import: do you support both online (KMIP/PKCS#12) and offline wrapped key import? If offline, what envelope format and courier expectations do you have?

2) HSM hosting options: can Redwood operate with a customer-managed HSM inside our VPC (we need cryptographic operations to occur in a customer-controlled HSM) vs. Redwood-managed HSM? What network connectivity options exist (VPC peering, PrivateLink, IPsec)?

3) Rotation: what is the default rotation cadence for master keys and data keys? How are rotations orchestrated and can we opt-in to automatic rotation with signed logs?

4) TLS and client authentication: which TLS versions / cipher suites do you support? Do you enforce mutual TLS for inter-service and HSM connections?

5) Audit logs & evidence: what logging/audit exports are available (CloudTrail, syslog, SIEM integration), and what attestations/third-party reports can you provide?

We attached the crypto appendix from our RFI. If you can send a short network playbook and a rotation template by EOD Wednesday that would help expedite procurement.

Thanks,
Priya Ramesh
Senior Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health

(attachment: nimbus_crypto_appendix_v3.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cryptography section clarifications / request for network diagram

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a short "network_playbook" + a rotation template and our attestation summary to this thread. Aditya (engineering) and Priyom (security) are looped in for any deep-dive follow ups.

Summary answers (TL;DR):
- BYOK import: we support online KMIP imports and PKCS#12 for wrapping keys, and an offline wrapped-key import workflow (customer provides wrapped key file encrypted with our node public key; chain-of-custody recommended). Offline imports use AES-KW + RSA-OAEP envelope patterns — see attachment for steps.
- HSM hosting: three supported patterns: (1) Customer-managed HSM in their VPC (cryptographic ops stay in customer HSM), (2) Customer-provisioned HSM hosted in vendor-managed colo with direct private connectivity, (3) Redwood-managed HSM cluster. We support VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink, and IPsec tunnels for connectivity; we can also support direct cross-account CloudHSM clusters when needed.
- Rotation: default data-key rotation is 90 days; tenant master keys are rotated on request or per contract (typical 365-day cadence). Rotations are orchestrated via signed rotation jobs; each rotation creates an immutable audit record and a verifiable signature bundle.
- TLS / mutual auth: we support TLS 1.2 and 1.3, prefer 1.3 with AEAD ciphers (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). Mutual TLS is enforced for HSM management endpoints and recommended for PrivateLink connections.
- Audit & evidence: logs exported to customer-controlled S3 or SIEM endpoints, CloudTrail-compatible events for API actions, and HSM audit trails retained per contract. SOC 2 Type II and recent vendor attestation summaries are available under NDA (attached).

Next steps: if you can share a preferred time for a 30-45 minute technical workshop we will bring a network diagram and a step-by-step BYOK playbook. In the meantime I'm attaching: redwood_network_playbook.pdf, rotation_schedule_template.xlsx, attestation_summary_2027-04.pdf.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick reply and attachments — helpful. A couple of specific follow-ups from our security team before the workshop:

1) For the customer-managed HSM option, can you confirm that cryptographic operations (sign/encrypt/decrypt) are executed inside the customer's HSM and that Redwood never receives unwrapped key material? Is there any metadata about keys that is stored in your control plane?

2) For KMIP over TLS: do you support mutual authentication at the KMIP layer (client certs) and is KMIP proxied through Redwood's control plane or a direct channel from Redwood compute to the customer HSM?

3) Key rotation proofs: can you provide an example of the "verifiable signature bundle" you mentioned? We need to validate rotation events in our KMS audit tooling.

4) Logs: what is the maximum retention you offer for HSM audit trails and do you support real-time forwarding to our SIEM (syslog/HTTPS ingest)?

If you can confirm these points in writing that will help us clear this stage — we can follow up in the technical workshop for details.

Regards,
Sam Turner
Security Engineer, Nimbus Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <security_engineer@nimbushealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Ramesh <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 May 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cryptography section clarifications / request for network diagram

Sam — thanks for the excellent follow-ups. I'll answer each point succinctly and link to artifacts in Drive for the workshop.

1) Customer-managed HSM ops and key material
- Confirmed: when customers choose the "Customer-managed HSM in VPC" option, all crypto primitives execute inside the customer's HSM. Redwood's compute nodes call the HSM over the customer-provided private connectivity; unwrapped key material never traverses Redwood's control plane.
- Metadata stored: Redwood stores only non-sensitive key metadata (key_id, algorithm, creation_ts, rotation_policy, and a hashed key fingerprint). The actual key material, wrapped keys, and key encryption keys remain under customer control.

2) KMIP over TLS and mutual auth
- We support KMIP 2.0 over TLS with mutual certificate authentication for KMIP endpoints. Connections are established directly from Redwood runtime compute into the customer's HSM endpoint (no proxying through the public control plane) when the customer-hosted pattern is used. When customers opt for Redwood-managed HSM we broker KMIP in a hardened VLAN but still use mutual TLS and client certs.

3) Rotation proofs (verifiable signature bundle)
- Rotation jobs produce a signed bundle that includes: rotation_job_id, previous_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint, timestamp, operator_cert_chain, and an HSM-signed assertion (where available) that the wrap/unwrap occurred inside the HSM. The bundle is signed with an RSA-2048 operator key and includes the operator certificate chain. Example artifact (redacted) is in Drive: the bundle is a small JSON file with a PKCS#7 signature wrapper; we can export in a format compatible with your ingestion tooling.

4) Logs and retention
- HSM audit trail retention: configurable up to 7 years (default 1 year) depending on contract. We support real-time forwarding to customer SIEM via syslog over TLS, HTTPS webhook, or by pushing to a customer-owned S3 bucket. CloudTrail-compatible API logs are available with a guaranteed 90-day retention on hosted and configurable retention for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Attachments & links: the network diagram + example rotation bundle are in the shared Drive folder (link in my signature). For the workshop we recommend: (a) a short session to validate connectivity options and IP allowlists and (b) a second session for a live BYOK import demo into a pre-provisioned CloudHSM cluster.

Action items:
- Marissa: propose two 30-45min slots for the tech workshop (we will bring an engineer + security engineer)
- Priya/Sam: share preferred calendar windows and any IP ranges for allowlist pre-check

Thanks,
